result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say to keep the identity. A keeps its suggestions small: refine the spacing, fix the digital presence, and check with customers before touching the sign. It also asks what evidence would justify a bigger change. B explains better why a gradient would fail on the black receipt version and at small sizes, but then adds a sans-serif supporting layer, a new graphic device and layout rules, which drifts toward a redesign. It also wrongly assumes a heavy slab has hairlines that need fixing. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say to keep the identity. B stays focused: it names what already works, keeps changes small (spacing, letterforms, digital presence) and says what would justify a bigger change, such as newcomers thinking the store looks closed, along with the cost of replacing physical items. A drifts toward a redesign with a new supporting typeface, a graphic device and layout rules, and it wrongly treats a heavy slab serif as having fragile hairlines.
